Ms. Shanti Tiwari - Panel Lawyer for respondent/State.

Order 
This is second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.176/2023 dated 15.04.2023 registered at Police Station Chhipawada District Harda for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the statement of victim has been recorded before the trial Court.
Victim has turned hostile.
She has not supported the allegation levelled against the present applicant.

In paragraph 7, the victim has disclosed that she was manhandled at the behest of her parent as well as Mama (uncle) as there were undue pressure upon the victim to enter into wedlock with an old aged person and therefore, the victim ran away from her parental house and went to Indore where she stayed in temple.

It is contended by the counsel that her testimony make it NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12231 2 MCRC-9431-2025 abundantly clear that the present applicant has been falsely implicated, he is aged about 21 years, the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer and submitted that offence has been committed upon the victim.

DNA report is positive and therefore, the testimony of the prosecutrix recorded before the trial Court, automatic becomes suspicious as the prosecutrix is denying the factum of relationship with the present applicant.

Hence, counsel submits that no case Umesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182544045/
1 for grant of bail is made out.

sentences.text:
4. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
5.
Having considered the submission perusal of record and the fact that so far as the present applicant is concerned, prosecutrix has not alleged anything against the present applicant.
She has not supported the allegations levelled by the prosecution.
The applicant is aged about 21 years and he is in custody since 29.01.2024.
Thus, taking into consideration the prolong period of custody and also age of the applicant, this Court is of the considered view that it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

7. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12231 3 MCRC-9431-2025 2023.
8.
Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
